jobs.title: Environmental Geologist
jobs.description:
Company Overview

EKI Environment & Water, Inc. (EKI) is an employee-owned environmental, water resources, and engineering consulting firm serving private- and public-sector clients throughout the United States. If you are interested in improving the environment and advancing your career, then EKI is the place for you.

ROLE

The Environmental Geologist position reports to their Team Leader (TL) and is a hands-on role that involves supporting site characterization, environmental investigation, remediation, construction, and operations projects for industrial, commercial, and municipal clients. Day-to-day work focuses on planning site investigations, collecting environmental samples and data, making field observations, overseeing contractors, logging soil boreholes, assessing and interpreting subsurface stratigraphy by preparing geologic cross sections, evaluating data and preparing environmental reports and technical documents.

Primary Duties & Responsibilities

Your responsibilities may include, but will not be limited to the following:

Prepare for and plan field work, including preparation of documentation and equipment, participation in planning meetings with project teams, coordination with laboratories, and scheduling the work of subcontractors
Conduct field work at project sites including:
Soil, groundwater, soil vapor, and indoor air sampling
Site inspections
Observe and document the work of other parties
Construction, operation, monitoring, and maintenance of remedial systems
Manage drillers and subcontractors
Construction management

Review and follow project work plans and standard procedures to ensure samples and data are collected and handled correctly
Document field work by preparing detailed field notes, borehole logs, and photo logs
Collate, tabulate, and interpret data and develop conceptual site models to support identification of contaminant sources and routes of exposure to human health and the environment
Work with senior staff to prepare environmental investigation work plans, reports, and costs for the investigation and remediation of hazardous waste sites and brownfields
Perform Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) compliance audits and implement follow-up corrective actions to ensure compliance with federal, state, and local regulations and permits
Implement stormwater compliance projects under the California Industrial General Permit for clients in a range of industries, including pollutant source assessments, identification of stormwater best management practices (BMPs) for implementation, design of advanced BMPs for stormwater treatment, and preparation of Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plans and Exceedance Response Action reports
Manage project schedules
Other duties as required

Qualifications & Requirements

Education

Bachelor’s degree in Geology, Environmental Science, or similar degree program; Master’s degree preferred

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

Two (2) years of experience preferred as a geologist involved with site investigation and remediation planning and implementation
Ability to work towards state licensing preferred
Strong technical and mechanical skills
Effective communication skills, both written and oral
Comfortable working outdoors in physically demanding environments and variable weather conditions
Ability to calibrate, repair, troubleshoot, and maintain field equipment and instruments
Ability to work safely and effectively around construction equipment, drilling operations, utilities, and industrial facilities
Geologist-In-Training certification preferred but not required
OSHA HAZWOPER 40-hour training preferred but not required
Experience with ESRI ArcGIS Pro preferred but not required

Competencies

Strong work ethic, reliability, attention to detail, and commitment to safety
Comfortable adapting to changing field conditions and priorities
Must have ability to multi-task, stay organized, work independently, and collaborate with various project teams
Must have a great attitude and eagerness to learn
Must have a current valid driver’s license and a clean driving record
Strong desire to grow personally as well as professionally

Physical Demands & Work Environment

Work in a fast-paced environment with high-volume workload and frequent short deadlines
Perform physically active outdoor work involving lifting, carrying, climbing, digging, tool operation, equipment setup, and material handling
Work safely around drilling equipment, excavation activities, construction sites, industrial operations, traffic, and active remediation systems
Frequently load, unload, transport, and organize tools, supplies, personal protective and sampling equipment
Work in muddy, dusty, noisy, hot, cold, wet, or otherwise challenging field conditions
Obtain medical clearance to work on hazardous waste site(s)
Lift up to 35 lbs
Stand, sit, bend, and stoop for extended periods during field work
With or without accommodation, work in outdoor environments with uneven terrain, variable outdoor conditions including heat, noise, and/or chemicals
Work in an environment with heavy, dangerous moving equipment
Work up to 10- to 12-hour days when field conditions require it
Maintain OSHA HAZWOPER and other applicable certifications including but not limited to ladder safety training, fall arrest training, etc.
Wear personal protective equipment (PPE) as needed, such as safety glasses, hard hat, boots, respirator, and hearing protection
Use hand and powered tools to install field sampling devices, to conduct well and probe sampling, or to remove nuts and bolts on well and probe vaults, etc.
Ability to assess the accuracy, neatness, and thoroughness of the work assigned

Travel Requirements

Must be able to travel for client meetings, site visits, and field work up to 75% of the time, predominantly within the Bay Area and occasionally outside the Bay Area

As an employee-owned firm, EKI offers a unique company culture with a corporate commitment to maintaining a positive work/life experience. EKI provides excellent compensation and comprehensive benefits packages, including career advancement opportunities, outstanding training opportunities, incentive compensation including bonuses, retirement benefits through an Employee Stock Ownership Program (ESOP) and 401(k) profit-sharing contributions, and group medical, vision, and dental benefits.

EKI Environment & Water, Inc is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration without regard to: race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity, genetic information, national origin, age (40 or older), disability, marital status, political affiliation, or military service.

jobs.description:
Job Description

Stanford University Department of Biomedical Data Science has an excellent opportunity available for a candidate interested in single-cell genomics, open science, and big data management as a part of the Lattice team.

Single-cell genomics has led to many recent advancements in our understanding of biological processes, development, and disease. The field continues to see explosive growth in data generation, and simultaneously, AI and ML models are offering increasingly powerful mechanisms to extract insights for the vast amounts of data. As the field continues to accelerate, effective data coordination and standardization become more critical to maximize the value of the data.

The Lattice team aims to accelerate scientific discovery by extending the lifecycle of data generated by the single-cell community. By sharing data in alignment with FAIR principles, they can be readily available for various reuse cases like large-scale data integrations, AI model training, and hypothesis generation. Lattice achieves this, in part, as the Submission Team for CZ CELLxGENE Discover, an open database and visualization platform for single-cell genomic data developed by Biohub. The Lattice team, along with computational biologists and software developers at Biohub, sets requirements for data hosted at CELLxGENE and collaborates with researchers to populate the CELLxGENE data corpus.

Additionally, Lattice team members are stewards for researchers funded directly by Biohub, most notably through their Billion Cells Project initiative. We collaborate with researchers to translate their experimental protocols into standardized metadata, work with industry partners to ensure accurate data processing and delivery, and ultimately, deliver the data to the scientific community.

The Research Data Analyst will join a small team of Ph.D. biologists, computational biologists, and experienced database managers in the GECKO (GEne Curation and KnOwledge) Group, and will work closely with external researchers and software developers. To ensure data are described by sufficient metadata, formatted in an interoperable manner, and error-free, the successful candidate will remain current on single-cell experimental methods and bioinformatics tools through published literature, attending scientific conferences and workshops, and building relationships with researchers in the community. They will distill learnings into schema specifications, quality assurance checks, or other data resource requirements and features that will improve the usability of data to researchers worldwide. We look forward to adding a motivated Research Data Analyst to be a valued contributor towards our mission as a part of this impactful project

Responsibilities

Core Duties
:

Collect, manage and clean datasets.
Employ new and existing tools to interpret, analyze, and visualize multivariate relationships in data.
Create databases and reports, develop algorithms and statistical models, and perform statistical analyses appropriate to data and reporting requirements.
Use system reports and analyses to identify potentially problematic data, make corrections, and determine root cause for data problems from input errors or inadequate field edits, and suggest possible solutions.
Develop reports, charts, graphs and tables for use by investigators and for publication and presentation.
Analyze data processes in documentation.
Collaborate with faculty and research staff on data collection and analysis methods.
Provide documentation based on audit and reporting criteria to investigators and research staff.
Communicate with government officials, grant agencies and industry representatives.

Bachelor's degree or a combination of education and relevant experience.

Minimum Experience

Experience in a quantitative discipline such as economics, finance, statistics or engineering.

Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

Substantial experience with MS Office and analytical programs.
Strong writing and analytical skills.
Ability to prioritize workload.

Overview

Company Description

As a Senior Data Analyst on the Corporate Intelligence Platform team, you will be the analytic engine and data steward ensuring CIP’s outputs are accurate, reliable, and meaningful. This role is all about making our data sing – you will dive deep into enterprise source systems (HR, Finance, project tracking, etc.) to understand and document data, then shape it into trusted analytical datasets and dashboards that drive executive decisions. By painstakingly validating data quality, defining core metrics, and building intuitive dashboard views, you’ll transform raw data into insights that Epsilon’s leaders rely on. Your work will bridge the gap between data engineering and business teams, ensuring that CIP not only centralizes data but also delivers answers to key business questions with confidence and clarity.

Responsibilities

Source Data Mastery: Become the subject-matter expert on CIP’s source data. Work with IT and system owners to map out all relevant fields and data flows from our internal systems (e.g., HRIS, financial databases, project management tools) into the CIP environment. Document data definitions, schemas, and business logic, making sure the team and end-users understand the context and limitations of each data source. Identify any data gaps or integrity issues early and recommend solutions or workarounds.
Refined Data Products & Metrics: Collaborate with data engineers and the product manager to transform raw data into business-ready “Silver” and “Gold” layer datasets. Validate that data cleansing and transformation rules produce accurate results. Help design dimensional data models and aggregated views that support common analytics needs (for example, workforce cost by product/initiative, project delivery timelines, or revenue by product). Ensure each curated dataset has clear business context, defined metrics, and documentation so that it’s immediately useful and trustworthy for analysis.
Metrics Definition & Consistency: Define and maintain the catalog of key business metrics and KPIs within CIP. Work with partners in Finance, Product, and Operations to agree on a single definition for critical measures (e.g., “fully-loaded cost”, “utilization rate”, “bookings vs revenue”) and implement these calculations in CIP’s data models. Create and manage a semantic layer or metrics repository that ensures all reports and dashboards use consistent formulas. By driving this consistency and clarity, you’ll prevent divergent numbers and solidify CIP’s reputation as the single source of truth for internal analytics.
Data Quality & Validation: Establish rigorous data quality checks to catch issues like missing data, inconsistencies, or anomalies. Regularly reconcile CIP’s aggregated results with source system records (e.g., compare CIP’s finance totals with official finance system outputs) to ensure everything lines up. Investigate discrepancies to find root causes – whether a pipeline issue, data entry error, or definition mismatch – and work with data engineers to implement fixes. You will also monitor data freshness and reliability, giving partners confidence that CIP’s insights are accurate and up-to-date.
Analytics & Dashboard Development: Design and deliver insightful analytics and dashboards on top of CIP’s datasets. Use your data exploration skills (e.g., advanced SQL in Databricks SQL/GenAI tools) to answer ad-hoc executive questions and to shape the content of dashboards. SQL & Data Proficiency: You are a SQL expert – comfortable writing advanced queries to join, aggregate, and analyze data. You may have some experience with Python or data visualization tools, and you’re always eager to learn new technologies (including using AI tools to accelerate data analysis).
Detail-Oriented & Quality-Focused: You are obsessed with data accuracy and consistency. You have experience setting up data quality checks, verifying results against source systems, and ensuring that dashboards are error-free. You understand the importance of data governance, and you naturally document your work so others can trust and build upon it.
Metrics & Business Savvy: You understand business metrics and can engage with business partners to refine them. You excel at asking the right questions to ensure a metric truly reflects business reality. Your analytical skills help you connect the dots between data points and business outcomes, so you can support collaborators in interpreting results and finding opportunities or issues.
Collaborative & Communicative: You work best in a team environment, closely partnering with data engineers, product managers, and other analysts. You can communicate complex data findings in simple terms, helping non-technical colleagues understand what the numbers mean and why they matter.
Education: Bachelor’s degree in a quantitative field (Statistics, Computer Science, Data Analytics, Finance, etc.) or equivalent experience. Professional certifications or training in data analysis/BI (e.g., data analytics certifications) are a plus.

Stanford University Department of Biomedical Data Science has an excellent opportunity available for a candidate interested in single-cell genomics, open science, and big data management as a part of the Lattice team.

Single-cell genomics has led to many recent advancements in our understanding of biological processes, development, and disease. The field continues to see explosive growth in data generation, and simultaneously, AI and ML models are offering increasingly powerful mechanisms to extract insights for the vast amounts of data. As the field continues to accelerate, effective data coordination and standardization become more critical to maximize the value of the data.

The Lattice team aims to accelerate scientific discovery by extending the lifecycle of data generated by the single-cell community. By sharing data in alignment with FAIR principles, they can be readily available for various reuse cases like large-scale data integrations, AI model training, and hypothesis generation. Lattice achieves this, in part, as the Submission Team for CZ CELLxGENE Discover, an open database and visualization platform for single-cell genomic data developed by Biohub. The Lattice team, along with computational biologists and software developers at Biohub, sets requirements for data hosted at CELLxGENE and collaborates with researchers to populate the CELLxGENE data corpus.

Additionally, Lattice team members are stewards for researchers funded directly by Biohub, most notably through their Billion Cells Project initiative. We collaborate with researchers to translate their experimental protocols into standardized metadata, work with industry partners to ensure accurate data processing and delivery, and ultimately, deliver the data to the scientific community.

The Research Data Analyst will join a small team of Ph.D. biologists, computational biologists, and experienced database managers in the GECKO (GEne Curation and KnOwledge) Group, and will work closely with external researchers and software developers. To ensure data are described by sufficient metadata, formatted in an interoperable manner, and error-free, the successful candidate will remain current on single-cell experimental methods and bioinformatics tools through published literature, attending scientific conferences and workshops, and building relationships with researchers in the community. Overview

Company Description

As a Senior Data Analyst on the Corporate Intelligence Platform team, you will be the analytic engine and data steward ensuring CIP’s outputs are accurate, reliable, and meaningful. This role is all about making our data sing – you will dive deep into enterprise source systems (HR, Finance, project tracking, etc.) to understand and document data, then shape it into trusted analytical datasets and dashboards that drive executive decisions. By painstakingly validating data quality, defining core metrics, and building intuitive dashboard views, you’ll transform raw data into insights that Epsilon’s leaders rely on. Your work will bridge the gap between data engineering and business teams, ensuring that CIP not only centralizes data but also delivers answers to key business questions with confidence and clarity.

Responsibilities

Source Data Mastery: Become the subject-matter expert on CIP’s source data. Work with IT and system owners to map out all relevant fields and data flows from our internal systems (e.g., HRIS, financial databases, project management tools) into the CIP environment. Document data definitions, schemas, and business logic, making sure the team and end-users understand the context and limitations of each data source. Identify any data gaps or integrity issues early and recommend solutions or workarounds.
Refined Data Products & Metrics: Collaborate with data engineers and the product manager to transform raw data into business-ready “Silver” and “Gold” layer datasets. Validate that data cleansing and transformation rules produce accurate results. Help design dimensional data models and aggregated views that support common analytics needs (for example, workforce cost by product/initiative, project delivery timelines, or revenue by product). Ensure each curated dataset has clear business context, defined metrics, and documentation so that it’s immediately useful and trustworthy for analysis.
Metrics Definition & Consistency: Define and maintain the catalog of key business metrics and KPIs within CIP. Work with partners in Finance, Product, and Operations to agree on a single definition for critical measures (e.g., “fully-loaded cost”, “utilization rate”, “bookings vs revenue”) and implement these calculations in CIP’s data models. Create and manage a semantic layer or metrics repository that ensures all reports and dashboards use consistent formulas. By driving this consistency and clarity, you’ll prevent divergent numbers and solidify CIP’s reputation as the single source of truth for internal analytics.
Data Quality & Validation: Establish rigorous data quality checks to catch issues like missing data, inconsistencies, or anomalies. Regularly reconcile CIP’s aggregated results with source system records (e.g., compare CIP’s finance totals with official finance system outputs) to ensure everything lines up. Investigate discrepancies to find root causes – whether a pipeline issue, data entry error, or definition mismatch – and work with data engineers to implement fixes. You will also monitor data freshness and reliability, giving partners confidence that CIP’s insights are accurate and up-to-date.
Analytics & Dashboard Development: Design and deliver insightful analytics and dashboards on top of CIP’s datasets. Use your data exploration skills (e.g., advanced SQL in Databricks SQL/GenAI tools) to answer ad-hoc executive questions and to shape the content of dashboards. For example, you might build a dashboard that highlights key product investment metrics or perform analyses to support long-term planning discussions.

Qualifications

Analytical Expert: You have 5+ years of experience as a data analyst, business intelligence analyst, or similar role, working with large-scale data sets and complex business metrics. You have a strong track record of turning data into insights used by business teams, and you’re excited by the challenge of making sense of diverse internal data.
SQL & Data Proficiency: You are a SQL expert – comfortable writing advanced queries to join, aggregate, and analyze data. You have hands-on experience with modern data platforms (Databricks or similar required) and a solid understanding of data warehouse/lake concepts (familiarity with Lakehouse/Delta Lake, medallion architectures). You may have some experience with Python or data visualization tools, and you’re always eager to learn new technologies (including using AI tools to accelerate data analysis).
Detail-Oriented & Quality-Focused: You are obsessed with data accuracy and consistency. You have experience setting up data quality checks, verifying results against source systems, and ensuring that dashboards are error-free. You understand the importance of data governance, and you naturally document your work so others can trust and build upon it.
Metrics & Business Savvy: You understand business metrics and can engage with business partners to refine them. You excel at asking the right questions to ensure a metric truly reflects business reality. Your analytical skills help you connect the dots between data points and business outcomes, so you can support collaborators in interpreting results and finding opportunities or issues.
Collaborative & Communicative: You work best in a team environment, closely partnering with data engineers, product managers, and other analysts. You can communicate complex data findings in simple terms, helping non-technical colleagues understand what the numbers mean and why they matter.
Education: Bachelor’s degree in a quantitative field (Statistics, Computer Science, Data Analytics, Finance, etc.) or equivalent experience. Professional certifications or training in data analysis/BI (e.g., data analytics certifications) are a plus.

Primary Function

The Construction Project Coordinator supports Dacon’s project managers and field leadership by coordinating construction activities, managing project documentation, and facilitating communication across internal teams, subcontractors, and suppliers. This role ensures construction projects progress on schedule and within budget through proactive scheduling support, procurement coordination, compliance tracking, and administrative oversight. The position will be based in our Deer Park, Texas office located at 1300 Underwood Rd, Deer Park, TX 77536.

Duties & Responsibilities

Employee may be called upon to perform any or all of the following functions:

Project Coordination & Scheduling

Assist in planning and scheduling construction activities in coordination with project managers and field leadership.
Coordinate timelines between field leadership, subcontractors, suppliers, and the Project Management team.
Monitor project progress and flag delays, conflicts, or issues to the appropriate stakeholders.
Help ensure project milestones and deadlines are met through proactive tracking and follow-up.

Documentation & Reporting

Assemble project documentation packages for field leadership, including drawings, schedules, Site-Specific Execution Plans (SEPs), and contracts.
Track and organize change orders; gather timesheets from the General Foreman and coordinate with Accounting to apply accurate costs.
Ensure project files are maintained in accordance with company standards and document control procedures.

Communication & Stakeholder Management

Act as a liaison between project managers, field leadership, and site teams to ensure alignment on project priorities and status.
Ensure clear and timely communication across all parties involved in project execution.

Procurement & Resource Coordination

Assist with sourcing materials and tracking deliveries to support construction schedules.
Coordinate with vendors and suppliers to ensure timely availability of materials and equipment.

Compliance & Safety Support

Obtain safety requirements from clients, including but not limited to drug screening, safety course requirements, badging, and specialty safety equipment.
Verify that Master Service Agreements (MSAs) and Certificates of Insurance (COIs) are current and up to date.

Administrative Support

Maintain organized project files in both digital and physical formats.
Support contract administration and document control systems.
Assist the General Foreman with day-to-day operational and administrative tasks.
Perform special projects and complete other duties as assigned or requested.

Enable project managers and field leadership to focus on execution by proactively managing schedules, documentation, and stakeholder communication.
Reduce project risk by ensuring 811 tickets, safety requirements, MSAs, and COIs are tracked and current before work begins.
Improve cost accuracy by coordinating change order tracking, timesheet collection, and cost application with Accounting.
Support on-time material delivery and resource availability through effective vendor and supplier coordination.
Strengthen Dacon’s project documentation standards, ensuring consistent and accessible records across all active projects.

Ready to thrive in a dynamic, high-energy environment? Join our Lung Screening Program Team and bring your exceptional talents to a team that makes a real impact—every single day.

You would be responsible for the daily operations, including staff and workflow, for the Lung Cancer Screening Program (LCSP). Supports all aspects of the LCSP database including data extraction and entry, statistical reporting, and enhancements, including participating in community outreach events. Collaborates with Thoracic Surgery, Radiology, Pulmonary, Oncology and other departments to support all efforts related to guiding patients through the screening process, utilizing best practices. Works with referring physician offices and clinics to manage initial referrals through follow-up imaging tests and workup for all suspicious findings.

What You Will Do

Guides patients through the screening, enrollment, and appointment process and works together with program staff to Schedule appointments and diagnostic studies, obtain prior authorizations and track status of patients in database.
Performs program Quality assessment checks, audits, and reviews.
Aids in developing and driving initiatives to eliminate barriers to the lung cancer screening program. Provides assistance and collaboration to establish processes and standards that ensure consistent patient scheduling including follow up diagnostic imaging exams.
Conducts outreach with potential referring providers and works collaboratively with physician liaisons and related departments to increase referrals to the program.
Communicates with referring physicians regarding patient appropriateness for program and coordinates information with referral services.
Distributes patient letters, provides follow-up and confirmation calls and responsible for collecting and maintaining patient responses to program surveys. Responsible for maintaining the LCSP database, which includes data entry, patient letters, patient management activities and statistical reporting.
Responsible for managing the National Lung Cancer Screening Registry including extracting data from operative reports, pathology reports and imaging and manually uploading into the ACR to maintain accreditation standards.
Prepares weekly program statistics. Provides updates on program activity, statistics, and recommendations for program enhancements.
Serves as an active member of the Lung Cancer Screening Program Steering committee and as an ad-hoc member to the Thoracic Tumor Board committee. Serves as an ad-hoc member to the Lung Cancer Tumor Board team.
Ensures all accreditation requirements are adhered to, gathers, and submits required data in a timely fashion.
Coordinates with Patient Financial Services and the Finance Department as needed. Assists in tracking the financial impact of program. Prepares analytical data as requested.
Helps plan and organize community outreach events, working collaboratively with THOfNE department such as Community Health and Wellness, Oncology, and other departments. Offsite work and hours may occasionally apply. Assists in the planning of specialized lung cancer and smoking cessation events and programs during key times of the year including lung cancer awareness month.
Provides cross-coverage to the thoracic surgery clinic and oncology clinic as needed.

Monday - Friday; hours can be flexible around start/end times

Minimum Qualifications

Minimally requires a high school diploma or equivalent. Associate’s degree in related field is preferred. Medical Assistant and/or certified tumor registrar (CTR) preferred.
A minimum of three (3) years of progressive relevant experience in a healthcare environment. Previous experience in Pulmonary Medicine, Oncology or Diagnostic Imaging preferred. Prior experience in scheduling preferred.
Advanced knowledge of computer systems, Microsoft office-Word, PowerPoint, Excel, etc. Requires exceptional data entry skills.
Strong organizational and interpersonal skills. Demonstrates attention to detail. Presentation skills required.
Strong customer service skills required. Excellent communication skills required to interact with all levels of Clinic personnel. Ability to take initiative and work independently with minimum supervision.
